title: Canonicalize rate-limit semantics, idempotency and error shapes for OpenAI compatibility layer
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customers integrating via the OpenAI-compat endpoint reported inconsistent rate-limit headers, divergent error shapes, and duplicate side-effects when clients retried non-idempotent requests. This PR harmonizes rate-limit semantics, enforces idempotency key handling for mutating endpoints, standardizes Retry-After behavior for streaming and non-streaming paths, and normalizes error bodies to follow OpenAI-compatible schema. Motivation: reduce accidental duplicate side-effects, make client retry logic deterministic, and improve compatibility for downstream SDKs that expect OpenAI-like errors. Changes: - Implement canonical RateLimitResponse object returned by middleware and populated into response headers and JSON body with fields x-ratelimit-limit/x-ratelimit-remaining/x-ratelimit-reset and Retry-After (seconds). - Centralize idempotency key validation in openai_compat/idempotency.py including strict key length/charset checks and a new 409 conflict path when a different result for same idempotency key exists. - Add persistent idempotency store backed by Redis with TTL aligned to model response window, and deterministic replay of stored responses (200/201/whatever original status). - Streaming stability: when a streaming request is rate-limited mid-stream, the server sends a final CRLF-delimited JSON error frame matching OpenAI streaming error conventions then closes the stream. - Retry-After semantics: when overloaded, server prefers 503 with Retry-After for transient cases, 429 when quota exhausted; both include consistent body and headers. - Error shapes: unify error payload to {"error":{"message":...,"type":...,"param":...,"code":...}} for all handlers. - Tool/function-calling: validate idempotency for tool-invoking chat completions and ensure tool side-effects are only executed once per idempotency key; added compensating rollback hooks for failures during replay. - Added integration tests covering idempotency replay, streaming Retry-After, and SDK compatibility scenarios. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] e2e streaming test, [x] documentation snippets updated, [x] added Linear ticket references, [x] added release notes entry.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: The overall approach looks good. Two questions: 1) Do we risk replaying sensitive side-effects by deterministically returning previous responses? 2) How long will items live in Redis?

Maya Chen (author): We added configurable TTL with sensible default 24 hours; teams can opt shorter. For sensitive side-effects we require explicit "safe_for_replay" flag on endpoints; tool invocations default to false unless caller opts in and provides compensating rollback handlers.
Priya Nair: Please add a migration note for Dedicated customers with existing idempotency behavior - will this change their previous dedupe semantics?
Maya Chen: Added docs and an opt-in flag 'compat.enable_legacy_idempotency' for Dedicated; default false. Noted in release notes.
Diego Ramirez: Suggest returning 409 with existing idempotency mismatch payload instead of 400 to be clearer to clients.
Maya Chen: Switched to 409 and added a small schema snippet showing the 'existing_response' metadata in the body (base64 for raw payload).

release_notes: Stabilize OpenAI-compatible error semantics: canonicalized rate-limit headers and JSON error shapes, deterministic idempotency replay for mutating endpoints, clarified Retry-After behavior for streaming and non-streaming requests. Dedicated customers: opt-in legacy mode available via config. See openai_compat.md for migration steps.
